data.long_meaning: Derived from the Sanskrit word 'Kishor', meaning the 'Lord of all senses'. In Hindu mythology, Kishore is a term used to describe Shiva as the Lord of all senses or the embodiment of sensual pleasure. The name Kishore carries the meaning “Lord of all senses” and is chosen by families in Hindu traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Sanskrit tradition and is also used in Hindi, Sanskrit, Marathi. Parents who choose Kishore usually hope their child will grow to embody lord of all senses and live with faith, good character and purpose.

It also evokes the God Shiva, a major deity in Hinduism, who is often worshipped as the god of all senses and the embodiment of happiness and bliss. In certain regions, Kishore is also a common name for boys, passing on the cultural richness of the name through generations.
data.spiritual_significance: In the spiritual context, the name 'Kishore' is closely associated with Lord Shiva, who is the embodiment of sensual pleasure and the universal giver of blessings. The name signifies the innate spiritual desire to connect with the divine essence within oneself and to experience the bliss of pure consciousness. By invoking the name 'Kishore', one can honor and remember the divine presence of Lord Shiva and seek his blessings for inner happiness and prosperity.
data.spiritual_symbolism: The name Kishore signifies youthfulness and vitality. It is derived from the Sanskrit words 'Kishor' meaning 'young' or 'youth' and 'Rama' meaning 'God'. Thus, Kishore represents the divine energy of youth in an individual, connected to the divine essence of God.
